hypothesis: The scored truth is by construction the set of faults absent from the competition catalogue. The USGS State Geologic Map Compilation is an independently compiled product, so a state-map fault that lies more than one kernel width (300 m) from every catalogue cell is a high-precision candidate for an expert-labelled 'new' fault.
mechanism: Historical H54-A hypothesis: source-provenance complement, then geometry. It buffers the competition catalogue, filters mapped traces using principal-axis geometry, and emits spaced dots. The earlier claimed benefit of pruning was inferred from owner-recorded, unreceipted board observations and must be treated as MODEL/PROXY context, not as an empirical organizer-confirmed result. The candidate uses the SGMC layer that also defines its only proxy target, so the proxy evaluation is circular.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: State geologic map compilation line work that is not a Quaternary fault: (a) pre-Quaternary (Tertiary) faults with no surface scarp, which appear on state maps but are not in the experts' label set; (b) non-fault linework -- dike and vein traces, lithologic contacts digitised as lines, and map neatlines; (c) mylonitic or metamorphic fabric boundaries. The linearity gate removes (b) and (c) only to the extent that they are blob-shaped or short; item (a) is NOT removed by anything in this design and is the main reason the artefact could underperform. A Quaternary viability gate was specified as the direct remedy (hypothesis H54-B) but was not run in this session.
